title: Exclusive labeling of direct and indirect pathway neurons in the mouse neostriatum by an adeno-associated virus vector with Cre/lox system
protocol: Disinfect instruments with 70% ethanol.
Fabricate a glass micropipette using a PC-100 puller set to heating value 73.5 and pulling force 125 g.
Aspirate 500 nL of AAV vector solution into the glass micropipette.
Mark the top surface with a permanent marker after aspirating 500 nL.
Aspirate an additional 200 nL of AAV vector solution.
Fixate an anesthetized mouse head with a stereotaxic instrument.
Perforate the skull using a hand drill.
Connect Picospritzer III to a high-pressure N2 cylinder.
Attach the glass micropipette to the holder of Picospritzer III.
Insert the micropipette into the brain.
Fold the tip with fine-tip tweezers.
Check under a microscope that the tip is 50–70 μm in diameter.
Dilute AAV2/1-E/SYN-FLEX-[pR-pG(r)] vector solution with PBS containing 2% (w/v) BSA to 1 × 10^11 infectious unit/mL.
Place the diluted solution on ice.
Aspirate 500 nL of an AAV vector solution on a Parafilm sheet through the tip of a glass micropipette using capillary action.
Mark the top surface of the solution with a permanent marker.
Aspirate 200 nL of a virus solution again (700 nL in total).
Aspirate the extra solution (e.g., 500 nL) and mark the level with a permanent marker.
Anesthetize a Drd1-Cre BAC transgenic mouse (8–16 weeks) by intraperitoneal injection of a mixture of medetomidine, midazolam, and butorphanol tartrate in saline.
Mount the anesthetized mouse into a stereotaxic instrument using an auxiliary ear bar.
Adjust the position of the mouth and nose fixing clamp until the lambda and bregma are equal in height.
Make an incision in the scalp with a scalpel along the midline to expose the skull.
Mark the skull above the CPu with a surgical marker-pen.
Thin the skull above the marked site using a hand drill with a steel hole cutter.
Remove the remaining bone using fine-tip tweezers to expose the surface of the brain.
Set the Picospritzer III to 40 psi injection pressure and 5 ms injection duration.
Eject a drop of virus solution from the tip of the glass micropipette to ensure it is not clogged.
Move the glass micropipette to the brain surface and slowly insert it into the target.
Pull the micropipette upward approximately 0.05 mm to make space for the virus solution to diffuse.
Inject the virus solution into the mouse CPu by pressure pulses through a glass micropipette attached to Picospritzer III for 5 min.
Leave the micropipette in place for 5 min, and then remove it slowly.
Close and sterilize the wound.
Administer antibiotics locally after closing the wound.
Recover the mouse from anesthesia by intraperitoneal injection of atipamezole (Antisedan; 1.5 mg/kg) in saline.
Maintain the mouse in specific pathogen-free conditions under a 12 h light/dark cycle with ad libitum access to food and water for 1 week after the AAV injection.
Anesthetize the mouse deeply by intraperitoneal injection of sodium pentobarbital (Somnopentyl; 200 mg/kg) in saline.
Open the thoracic cavity with surgical scissors.
Cut the right atrial appendage to bleed.
Insert a 22-gauge needle from the apex into the left ventricle of the heart.
Perfuse with 20 mL of PBS using a syringe for 3 min.
Perfuse with 20 mL of a fixative solution using another syringe at the same speed.
Remove the brain from the skull and place it in the same fixative solution.
Incubate the brain in the fixative solution for 12–24 h at 4°C.
Replace the fixative solution with 30% (w/v) sucrose in 0.1 M PB.
Gently shake the mixture for 1–2 days at 4°C to cryoprotect the brain tissue.
Approximately 30 min before sectioning, turn on the low temperature circulator and set it to 4°C.
Mount the brain tissue onto the stage of a freezing microtome with OCT compound.
Adjust the stage angle to keep the sagittal plane of the brain horizontal.
Set the electro-freezing component to −25°C.
Quickly freeze the brain tissue using dry ice powder and leave it in place for at least 5 minutes.
Cut the brain tissue into 20-μm-thick parasagittal sections.
Collect the sections with a paintbrush.
Store the collected sections in vials containing 0.02% sodium azide in 0.1 M PB.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of PBS for 10 minutes twice.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of PBS-X for 30 minutes.
Incubate the sections for 12–24 hours with a mixture of 20 μg/mL of chicken polyclonal anti-GFP antibody and 1 μg/mL of affinity-purified rabbit antibody against mRFP1 in 500 μL of PBS-XCD.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of PBS-X for 10 minutes twice.

Incubate the sections for 2 h with a mixture of 5 μg/mL of AlexaFluor (AF) 488-conjugated antibody against chicken IgY and 5 μg/mL of AF568-conjugated antibody against rabbit IgG in 500 μL of PBS-XCD.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of PBS-X for 20 min twice.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of PBS for 20 min twice.
Mount the sections onto APS-coated glass slides.
Apply a coverslip with a mounting medium for fluorescence microscopy.
Mix solutions A and B of ABC Elite kit at a ratio of 1:100 each in 500 μL of PBS-X.
Incubate the mixture for at least 30 min at 20°C–25°C with gentle shaking to form the avidin-biotinylated peroxidase complex (ABC).
Wash sections with 8 mL of PBS for 10 min twice.
Incubate sections for 30 min with 8 mL of 1% (v/v) H2O2 in PBS to inactivate endogenous peroxidase activity.
Wash sections with 8 mL of PBS-X for 10 min twice.
Incubate sections for 12–24 h with 0.1 μg/mL affinity-purified rabbit antibody against GFP or mRFP1 in 500 μL of PBS-XCD.
Wash sections with 8 mL of PBS-X for 10 min twice.
Incubate sections for 2 h with 10 μg/mL biotinylated goat antibody against rabbit IgG in 500 μL of PBS-XCD.
Wash sections with 8 mL of PBS-X for 10 min twice.
Incubate sections for 1 h with a 1:100-diluted avidin-biotinylated peroxidase complex (ABC) in 500 μL of PBS-X.
Wash sections with 8 mL of PBS-X for 10 min twice.
Wash sections with 8 mL of 0.1 M PB for 10 min twice.
Incubate sections for 5 min with a BT-GO reaction mixture containing 1:50,000-diluted BT solution, 3 μg/mL GO, and 1% BSA in 1 mL of 0.1 M PB.
Add 10 μL of β-D-glucose solution to achieve a final concentration of 2 mg/mL and mix the solution thoroughly.
Incubate the sections for 30 min.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of 0.1 M PB for 10 min.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of PBS-X for 10 min twice.
Incubate the sections for 1 h with 1/100-diluted ABC in 500 μL of PBS-X.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of PBS-X for 10 min twice.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of PBS for 10 min twice.
Incubate the sections for 30–60 min with 0.02% (w/v) DAB and 0.0001% (v/v) H2O2 in 8 mL of 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.6).
Check the progress of DAB deposition under the microscope.
Stop the reaction when a high signal-to-noise ratio is achieved.
Add additional H2O2 directly to the reaction solution if DAB deposition is weak and slow.
Wash the sections with 8 mL of PBS for 10 min three times.
Mount all the stained sections serially onto APS-coated glass slides.
Dry up the sections.
Soak the glass slides in ethanol-water mixtures of 30, 50, and 70% (v/v) for 30 min each.
Dip the slides into 95% (v/v) ethanol in water.
Soak the glass slides in 100% ethanol for 12–24 h.
Dip the glass slides into a xylene-ethanol mixture of 50% (v/v).
Soak the slides in 100% xylene for 12–24 h.
Coverslip the sections with a mounting medium for bright-field microscopy, NEW MX.
Observe the sections under a bright-field microscope, MICROPHOT-FXA.
Acquire a color image of the entire section using the digital slide scanner TOCO with a 10× objective lens.
Trace and digitize the axons of DAB-stained neurons on the images with a digital pen tablet and graphic software ADOBE ILLUSTRATOR CS3.
Observe sections with a bright field microscope to accurately reconstruct out-of-focus axons.
